drafter.private_reasoning: The Buyer has countered with a price that is well below our reservation price and is seeking to add an earn-out structure. Our bottom line is $38.5m, so we must move closer to that without signaling our reservation. There is value in encouraging a prompt, collaborative close due to our firms' relationship. I will counter with a significant price reduction to $40m (still well above our reservation but responsive to their move and signaling flexibility), and propose a capped, objective earn-out of up to $2m tied to clear EBITDA targets. For reps/indemnities, I will accept all core items but propose clarifying/capping language to limit open-ended exposure (e.g., knowledge qualifier for litigation, materiality thresholds, and a two-year survival period). I will add the requested tax and general indemnity clauses, subject to customary caps and baskets, thereby showing commerciality but also managing risk for Seller. The tone of the cover note should be positive and collaborative, inviting a call if more is needed.

In response, we have proposed substantial movement on headline price and included an earn-out element based on objective financial measures, ensuring interests remain aligned post-closing. We have also broadened the representations and warranties to address your concerns, and added both a tax indemnity and a general indemnity provision, with customary limitations to provide certainty for both sides.

Should you wish to discuss the earn-out mechanism or any of the liability caps in more detail, we are happy to arrange a call at your convenience. We look forward to your thoughts and to progressing swiftly towards completion.

Best regards,
Aldous Finch LLP

The payments shall be made annually following delivery of audited accounts, and any earn-out shortfall shall not be carried over to subsequent periods. 5. Indemnities. 
(a) The Seller shall indemnify the Buyer for any loss arising from breach of any representation or warranty set out in Section 3, subject to an aggregate cap equal to 20% of the Purchase Price and a minimum claim threshold of USD 100,000 (basket).
(b) The Seller shall indemnify the Buyer against any taxes arising up to the Closing Date imposed on the Target, except to the extent provided for in the latest financial statements or otherwise disclosed in writing to the Buyer.
Claims under this Section must be made within two (2) years following Closing, except for tax claims, which may be made for up to four (4) years following Closing or up to the applicable statutory limitation period, whichever is shorter.

probe.private_reasoning: In the first round, the Seller proposed a headline price of $45,000,000. In the second round, despite their cover note referencing 'substantial movement on headline price', the actual document tracked changes show the headline price lowering to $40,000,000 with an added earn-out of up to $2,000,000—making the maximum possible consideration $42,000,000. This constitutes a $3m drop, or 6.6%, off their original figure in a single round, which is a significant early move. Sellers who make substantial initial concessions often have more room to move. Additionally, highlighting the earn-out capped at $2m suggests they are distancing themselves from the $45m figure; they are now positioning $40m as the real base, $42m as 'stretch.' Their negotiation language—inviting discussion on fine-tuning liability caps and the earn-out—indicates a willingness to be flexible to get a deal done, and there is no show of 'take it or leave it' posturing. Since there is still no clear bottom line signaled, and the drop was large and early, they likely have room to go below $40m, especially if earn-out is retained (helpful for the Seller to 'save face'). Additionally, typical negotiation dynamics and the lack of deal-specific justifications anchoring $40m as a minimum also suggest flexibility. Thus, my best estimate is that the Seller's side would accept $38,000,000 headline, possibly with a $2m earn-out, if pressured.
